Steak King HK · Key visual

The Salmon Bar

One master image carries the campaign. Everything else is a crop of it with copy laid over the top. Strip every word out and it should still be unmistakably The Salmon Bar — that is the test a key visual has to pass, and it is what separates this from a campaign hero.

The idea

The Salmon Bar is a bar, so the key visual is a bar: one unbroken row of the six products on the landing page, shot dead overhead on a single surface, lit once, running under one coral rail, with the lockup set in thin type above it.

No crushed ice, no glass, no wet display. That is the supermarket — the $500, the thawed fish, the three middlemen — and it is what the landing page argues against. This counter is portioned, sealed and laid in order, which is the argument made as a picture: portioned before it ships, take two out, leave the rest.

The lockup is set per output, never baked into the plate, and no price ever goes near it. That is what lets a tight crop keep the type intact and lets the image survive a price change.

The device

ElementSpec
GroundWarm bone #F4F1EA. Warm, never a clinical or blue white — a cold white is what makes salmon read supermarket.
RailOne unbroken coral #EC7D55 rule under the row, full width, cut off by both frame edges. Never centred, never rounded, never tapered.
RowGroups separate, never overlapping, never touching. Even spacing, one shared centreline, one hard top light, real contact shadows.

The master and the crop set

One band, every email

The email hero band above is the finalised key visual and it is identical on all three launch sends. No send uses a cropped variant of it. The square, story and link-ad crops exist for paid only.

Using it

Do

  • Crop along the counter — any span between two groups
  • Keep the rail in every crop, with air beneath it
  • Lay copy on the ground between the lockup and the row
  • Scale down from the master; never re-render a span
  • Cut between groups, never through a piece of fish

Don't

  • Bake a price, an offer or a countdown into the image
  • Recolour the ground, or drop the row onto black
  • Add ice, garnish, boards, props or a second background
  • Move, thicken, round or centre the rail
  • Mix in a product shot from another set
